# Outline (story-repo, revision 2; answers idea-review #3 in story-repo)

Built from the objective, the idea's `Brief` (rev. 4) and `prior_work.md`. It says what to test and what each part of the paper must say. It does **not** fix any result: every claim below is a hypothesis with a stated way to fail, and the paper reports whichever outcome the experiments give.

## 0. Working title and one-paragraph story
**"How much shorter can a prediction-powered interval be? Headroom over PPI++ when labels, unlabeled data and the predictor are all fixed."**

Prediction-powered inference (PPI, PPI++) turns a fixed predictor into a valid interval for E[Y]. With n labels, N unlabeled records and f fixed, the only freedom left is (a) how the labels are used to build the control variate g(Z), and (b) how the interval is built from the estimate. The classical semi-supervised / missing-data theory gives a variance floor V* = σ²_res/n + V_g/(n+N). We (1) write the exact gap between PPI++ and that floor, (2) say when learning a calibrated g from the same n labels pays for itself (break-even n*), (3) measure the headroom on the nine ppi-python sets, a synthetic suite with known truth, and (4) map where shorter intervals exist, where they do not, and where any method fails. "PPI++ is already near the floor on most standard datasets" is an acceptable headline; so is "large gain on skewed or non-monotone cells". We claim no new efficiency principle and no "first" (Zhang–Brown–Cai 2019; Robins–Rotnitzky–Zhao 1994; Gronsbell et al. 2022 are credited).

**Target parameter (chosen and justified in the paper):** population mean E[Y]. Reason: shared by all nine sets, truth known when a pool is treated as the population, the floor has a closed form. Regression coefficient = extension, only after the mean story is complete.

## 1. Fixed in advance (before any run): arms, margin, grid, headline form

**Arms (named; the ladder and Table 1 use exactly these).**
T1 (f only): A0 labels-only (z/t; Wilson and Clopper-Pearson for binary Y); A1 PPI (λ=1, `ppi-python==0.2.3`); A2 PPI++ (same package; the baseline to beat; the free PPI→PPI++ gain V_g(1/N−1/M) sits in this step, and A2 is already the pooled linear estimator); A3 post-stratified PPI on f-bins (post hoc, labels fixed); A4 **PPI++ run on Yhat := ĝ(f)**, ĝ cross-fitted isotonic/spline (nearest published-plus-calibration rival); A5 the **instrument**: pooled cross-fitted calibrated estimator with its own SE (widths of A4 and A5 reported side by side, should agree); A6 A5 with data-driven selection of g among {PPI++, calibrated, flexible} and safeguard, selection inside the repeated-sampling loop on folds separate from variance estimation; A7 estimated floor (cross-fitted fit on the whole pool; not a valid interval, a ceiling on headroom).
T2 (f and X; census sets, alphafold indicators): B1 vector PPI++ (g = a + b′(f,X)) and OLS-adjusted mean (strongest linear baseline); B2 GBM-AIPW; B3 calibrated + X; B4 floor with X.

**Headline measure and margin (set now; analysis may not move it after seeing results).** Paired width ratio r = width(arm)/width(A2 PPI++) on the same draws, with 95% CI over repetitions. Per cell: **no gain** if the CI of r lies inside [0.98, 1.02]; **gain** if the CI upper bound < 0.95 and the arm is valid (win rule of the Brief); **small / undecided** otherwise. Because width ∝ n^{-1/2}, r also reads as an effective label saving 1 − r² (r=0.95 ≈ 10% fewer labels); the paper states both. For each dataset at its reference n it reports: r of the best valid arm (A5/A6, and B-arms for T2), and r at the estimated floor (A7), both with CIs. The abstract's answer to "how much shorter" is the range of these numbers across sets, with the sets where it is no-gain named.

shown.message:
`story-repo`'s Outline rev. 2 adopts all six changes I asked for in `story-repo`#3. One small point is left over.

- **What was adopted:**
  - The arms are named A0–A7 and B1–B4, including PPI++ on calibrated predictions and post-stratified PPI.
  - The no-gain and gain margins are fixed in advance. No gain means the 95% CI of the paired width ratio against PPI++ lies in [0.98, 1.02]. Gain means the CI upper bound is below 0.95 and the arm is valid.
  - The n-grid is log-spaced and must bracket the predicted break-even n.
  - Selection of g, with its safeguard, is now in the core experiments.
  - The outline has a compute plan, with the order in which to cut work, and a data fallback.
  - The headline results now lead the paper, ahead of the identity check.
- **Not taken literally:** only `ballots` has a natural n, so the other sets get a reference n stated before the runs. I accepted that.
- **Left over:** the headline reports the best valid arm per dataset, chosen after seeing results. That choice is biased toward a gain and is not fixed in advance. I commented on `story-repo`#3 asking for one headline arm per tier, with the best-of-arms ratio shown only as a descriptive ceiling.
- **My commitment issue:** `idea-review-repo`#2 now records both reviews as sent.

I'll re-review if the Outline or the Brief changes again, and when `paper-repo` sets the division of the work, I'll check that every objective requirement has an owner.
